correctness.rationale: Every trim accepted path has exactly two edges, giving three disjoint layers; private intermediate states are forced by mixed-letter exclusion. In any cactus three private middle states cannot share one accepting end vertex, since the resulting \(K_{2,3}\) violates edge-unique cycles. Pair-grouped four-cycles attain the lower bound. Trees forbid any shared accepting end, and planar K_{2,n} gives the unrestricted optimum. Equality forces one end per middle; for odd n, an attempted duplication would produce two 4-cycles sharing one start-edge. Exact isomorphism counts are perfect/near-perfect matching counts. Code enumerates canonical possibilities through n=5 and checks acceptance and the cactus criterion, but does not substitute for the infinite graph proof.

Kutrib--Malcher--Schneider study the different model of symmetric transitions. Targeted published research-index queries returned predominantly unrelated automata compression claims; accessible earlier mathematical claims were compared for semantic overlap. No directly implying prior claim identified, but historical equivalences remain possible.

value.rationale: The 2026 general representation theorem explicitly leaves the minimum state blow-up open. This provides a natural fully resolved growing-alphabet witness with strict exact separation of planar, cactus, and tree NFAs and rigidity/counting of every extremal cactus representation. It quantifies the tradeoff in the canonical \(K_{2,n}\) example; the exact \(n!/(2^k k!)\) optimum count reflects structural matching constraints rather than an arbitrary finite table. Scope limited to a natural language family, not an arbitrary-language conversion theorem.
